title: the chakras as a map, not a claim (science seat)
hook: two comments under a glowing chakra post, both sure, both missing something
carry: the chakras as a map, not a claim (science seat)
tomorrow: the old map starts with someone asleep at the bottom. who?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Sri Yantra in a shop and on an altar: made a home by a rite and by worship, not by its brass. Today the map moves into the body.

A wellness post scrolls past: rainbow wheels stacked up a meditating figure, glowing like traffic lights. Under it, two comments. One says a scan has never found a single one, so they're fake. The other says they're real, you just can't see them. Both commenters are completely sure, and the thread runs on and on, nobody moving an inch. Inside Hinduism there's an older version of this argument. It's calmer, and it's more interesting than the comments.
screen: `RAINBOW WHEELS ON A FEED.` → `FAKE, SAYS ONE COMMENT.` → `REAL, SAYS THE OTHER.`

segments.voice: Chakra is the Sanskrit word for a wheel or a circle. In tantric and yoga texts like the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana, it names centers placed along the spine, from its base to the crown of the head, pictured as lotuses for the meditating mind. So what are they? Inside the tradition there are two answers, and each deserves its best case. The first view: the chakras belong to the sukshma sharira, the subtle body, a real layer of a person that isn't made of flesh. A scanner can't find them because it's built to find tissue, and the subtle body was never said to be tissue. The texts' detail, petals and colors and sounds, reads to these readers like a report from people who looked. The second view: the texts read like instructions. Where to rest attention, what to picture, in what order. Like the Sri Yantra, the chakras are a map, and a map is tested by walking it, not by scanning for it. Now notice what the two agree on. Neither calls the chakras organs. Neither thinks a scan settles anything. The science seat, the lens this run uses, asks the map question, and it can hold the other view with respect. Either way, a scan answers a question nobody here was asking.
screen: `CHAKRA: A WHEEL, A CIRCLE.` · `ONE VIEW: A SUBTLE BODY.` · `ANOTHER VIEW: A MAP FOR ATTENTION.` · `NEITHER ONE SAYS ORGANS.` · then, large: `A MAP, NOT A CLAIM.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and a scrap of paper. Write one line giving the best case for the subtle-body view, then one line for the map view, each as if it were your own. Read the two lines back slowly, and let them sit side by side without picking a winner.
The chakras as a map: centers along the spine, pictured as lotuses, read in this run as a guide for attention rather than a claim about tissue.
